newsitem.title: UK: Union says private bus firms face strike threat.
newsitem.headline: Union says private bus firms face strike threat.

text.p: The Transport & General Workers Union (T&G) said on Monday that staff at Britain's three largest private bus companies would be willing to strike over pay and conditions.

In a statement, T&G said more than 90 percent of T&G members at Stagecoach Holdings Plc, Firstbus Plc and Cowie group Plc who voted in a ballot said they would be prepared to vote for industrial action.
The T&G said it would contemplate strike action as part of its campaign for a national minimum standards agreement.

"Since the privatization of bus services staff have had to endure a steady deterioration in conditions, with longer hours and lower pay," the T&G said. "Local negotiations are becoming more impossible as central bus managements increase financial restraints on subsidiaries."
T&G spokesman Graham Stevenson said the three largest companies could not "continue to refuse to meet the union at national level" now that it was armed with the results of a consultative ballot.

The T&G said 49 percent of its members at Stagecoach voted in the ballot, with 95 percent of those backing strike action. At Firstbus, 40 percent voted, with 91 percent saying they would back strike action and at Cowie, 41 percent of members voted, with 93 percent of those favouring strike action.
